title: Global AI optimism is widespread while adoption, trust, and worry remain unevenly distributed
source_unit: Gallup, AI Optimism Globally Widespread Despite Uneven Use, reporting ongoing Gallup research with Microsoft, 22 September 2026
geography: Adults in the first 37 countries completing 2026 fieldwork in an ongoing global study intended to cover 140 countries

denominator.unit: countries in the first completed fieldwork set

ai_awareness.unit: median percent of adults aware of AI across 37 countries

ever_use.unit: median percent who have ever used AI for work or personal purposes

never_use.unit: median percent who have never used AI

adoption_ladder.value: the share of adults generally declines at each step from awareness to ever-use to frequent use

observations.method: Gallup global survey research with Microsoft, summarized by country-level adoption, emotion, expected-impact, and trust measures.
observations.uncertainty: The article does not provide the full country-by-country questionnaire, sampling details, or a single pooled respondent denominator in the public summary; the medians are not a global population-weighted estimate.
observations.subgroup: Adults in the 37 countries completing the initial 2026 fieldwork wave.
observations.counterinterpretation: Awareness and self-reported use can reflect different definitions of AI, access conditions, recall, and social desirability across countries.

denominator.unit: illustrative country cases in the Gallup summary

singapore.value: 96% aware, 79% ever used, and 46% daily use

malawi.value: 12% aware, 3% ever used, and 1% daily use

infrastructure_gap.value: the adoption ladder is sharply shaped by country-level connectivity, capability, and access conditions

boundary.value: the two examples illustrate dispersion and are not a causal estimate of infrastructure effects

observations.method: Published descriptive comparison of country estimates from the Gallup/Microsoft study.
observations.uncertainty: The country comparison does not isolate income, education, language, connectivity, device access, labor-market structure, or policy as separate causes.
observations.subgroup: Adults in Singapore and Malawi as illustrative endpoints of the reported adoption range.
observations.counterinterpretation: Country differences may reflect survey timing, translation, measurement, or sample composition as well as real differences in access and use.

denominator.unit: countries in the first fieldwork wave

daily_life_optimism.unit: countries where a majority of AI-aware adults expected AI to improve their daily lives

country_optimism.unit: countries where optimists outnumbered pessimists about AI's effect on the country

country_majority.unit: countries where an absolute majority expected AI to mostly help their country

optimism_use_gap.value: positive expectations can be widespread even where firsthand use remains limited

observations.method: Gallup comparison of AI-aware adults' expected personal and national impact across countries.
observations.uncertainty: Expected impact is an attitude measure and does not establish later use, productivity, employment, welfare, or political effects.
observations.subgroup: Adults aware of AI in the 37-country fieldwork set.
observations.counterinterpretation: Optimism may reflect general future orientation, national narratives, or limited direct experience rather than informed evaluation of AI systems.

observations.period: 2026; AI accuracy trust and adoption frequency

denominator.unit: countries in the first fieldwork wave

accuracy_trust.unit: median percent of AI-aware adults trusting AI completely or a lot to provide accurate information

optimism_trust_order.value: in 35 of 37 countries, more people expected AI to help their country than trusted it to provide accurate information

frequency_gradient.value: trust in accuracy rises with frequency of use; in the United States, 45% of daily users versus 8% of never-users expressed high trust

causal_boundary.value: the study cannot establish whether use builds trust, trust drives use, or both are shaped by prior conditions

observations.method: Gallup cross-country descriptive analysis of AI-aware adults by self-reported use frequency and trust in accuracy.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not establish temporal order, instrument exposure, task-specific accuracy, or whether trust transfers into consequential decisions.
observations.subgroup: AI-aware adults, with a United States frequency-of-use illustration.
observations.counterinterpretation: Frequent users may be more trusting because they have greater digital literacy, occupational access, or selective exposure to useful tools rather than because use itself causes trust.

observations.period: 2026; AI emotion and high-income Western-country contrast

denominator.unit: countries in the first fieldwork wave

positive_emotion.unit: countries where positive emotions toward AI outweighed negative emotions

positive_median.unit: median percent reporting at least one positive emotion toward AI

negative_median.unit: median percent reporting at least one negative emotion toward AI

western_worry.value: wealthy Western countries combine relatively high use with some of the highest worry; in the United States, 74% of AI-aware adults reported worry

observations.method: Gallup comparison of self-reported AI emotions by country and use frequency.
observations.uncertainty: Emotions are contemporaneous self-reports and do not predict a fixed behavioral response, policy preference, or future adoption path.
observations.subgroup: AI-aware adults across 37 countries, with high-income Western-country comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Worry may coexist with experimentation, work dependence, or curiosity; it should not be treated as rejection or non-use.

related_sources.claim: Pew provides complementary cross-country evidence on AI views and perceived effects.
UNDP's human-development and AI-choice work provides complementary agency and capability context.

boundary: This record adds a global AI diffusion route from awareness through use frequency, expected impact, trust in accuracy, emotions, and unequal access. It is a published cross-country survey summary, not a pooled causal panel, usage telemetry, model-accuracy audit, employment study, or proof that trust causes adoption.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gallup article was reviewed for its 37-country frame, adoption ladder, country contrasts, optimism and trust comparisons, emotion measures, Western-country worry pattern, and stated causal limitations.
